title: Truncated valuation depth and sieve visibility
pvg_object: valuation coordinates visible only through prime powers not exceeding level D
ant_object: divisibility indicators 1_{d|n} for d<=D and sieve level
forward_translation: Prime-power divisibility up to D determines the truncated visible depths min(v_p(n),floor(log_p D)).
reverse_translation: The complete pointwise indicator family recovers the truncated profile, but not higher exponents.
preserved_information: visible support and exponent depth within the sieve window
lost_information: heights beyond D, large-prime coordinates, sign, phase, and additive order
trigger: The method accesses divisibility only up to a finite level.
typical_output: visible valuation profile and explicit information ceiling
error_or_wall: A sieve level is not a pointwise primality certificate.
required_certificate: Specify D, the sequence, weights, main-term model, and remainder norm.
positive_example: For n=72 and D=9, indicators of 2,4,8,3,9 recover v_2=3 and v_3=2 within the window.
counterexample: 72 and 2^5*3^2 look identical if D is too small to see the extra 2-adic height.
anti_overclaim: Truncated divisibility information cannot be promoted to full factorization.

title: Aggregate sieve data and noninjective information loss
pvg_object: population of individual truncated valuation profiles
ant_object: aggregate divisibility sums A_d=sum_{n in A}w_n 1_{d|n}
forward_translation: Aggregating pointwise profiles produces divisibility moments indexed by d.
reverse_translation: The map from populations to A_d generally has a nontrivial kernel; individual profiles are not recoverable.
preserved_information: selected divisibility moments and modeled local densities
lost_information: individual identities, joint profiles, sign, phase, ordering, and many correlations
trigger: A sieve argument replaces a sequence by its family of divisor sums.
typical_output: explicit kernel or statement of which observables remain identifiable
error_or_wall: Treating aggregate A_d as if it were pointwise valuation data is invalid.
required_certificate: Prove injectivity for the requested observable or exhibit the information-loss kernel.
positive_example: The sets {2,3} and {2,5} have the same aggregate A_2=1 but different pointwise profiles.
counterexample: Knowing only A_2 cannot determine which odd element accompanies the even element.
anti_overclaim: Aggregate agreement is weaker than profile reconstruction.
source_basis: Linear aggregation and classical sieve data

title: Two-block valuation interactions and Type I/II structure
pvg_object: splitting valuation mass into two multiplicative blocks beta+gamma
ant_object: bilinear sums and Type I/Type II estimates
forward_translation: A factorization n=mn routes coordinate mass into two blocks, producing bilinear coefficient interactions.
reverse_translation: A bilinear form describes weighted block interactions but usually not a unique geometric split.
preserved_information: two-factor interaction scale and coefficient structure
lost_information: unique factorization routing, higher-order interactions, and pointwise target purity
trigger: Linear divisibility information is insufficient and cancellation must occur between two factor ranges.
typical_output: bilinear cancellation certificate over specified ranges
error_or_wall: A geometric split does not provide cancellation; coefficient norms and range balance are decisive.
required_certificate: State coefficient bounds, ranges, normalization, and the exact bilinear estimate.
positive_example: A divisor split near sqrt(n) motivates a balanced Type II range.
counterexample: Counting possible splits without signs gives no cancellation estimate.
anti_overclaim: Bilinear geometry is routing, not a Type II bound.
source_basis: Classical bilinear forms in sieve theory

title: Support data versus parity, sign, and phase walls
ant_object: Möbius or Liouville sign, oscillatory phase, and parity obstruction
forward_translation: Unsigned valuation geometry can encode parity only if support cardinality modulo two is explicitly retained; aggregated support data often erase it.
reverse_translation: Sign or phase data require an oriented or decorated valuation observable, not merely a support set.
preserved_information: parity when the exact support count is retained pointwise
lost_information: sign after aggregation, complex phase, ordering, and cancellation patterns
trigger: A target requires distinguishing primes from almost-primes or proving sign cancellation.
typical_output: named missing certificate rather than a false geometric proof
error_or_wall: Positive sieve weights cannot generally distinguish parity of the number of prime factors.
required_certificate: Identify the source of sign or phase and prove a cancellation estimate beyond support counts.
positive_example: For squarefree n, mu(n)=(-1)^omega(n) if omega is retained exactly.
counterexample: The same unsigned divisor-density data can arise from sequences with opposite signs.
anti_overclaim: Support geometry alone does not break the sieve parity barrier.
source_basis: Classical parity phenomenon and sign-loss audits
